sections.Overview: Costco Wholesale Corporation operates membership warehouses and e-commerce sites internationally, focusing on offering low prices on a limited selection of nationally-branded and private-label products across a broad range of categories. The company achieves this by leveraging volume purchasing, efficient distribution, and reduced handling of merchandise in no-frills warehouse facilities, resulting in high sales volumes and rapid inventory turnover. Costco operates 939 warehouses worldwide as of August 30, 2026, primarily in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Japan, the U.K., Korea, Australia, Taiwan, China, Spain, France, Sweden, Iceland, and New Zealand. Their warehouses average approximately 148,000 square feet, designed for operational efficiency and inventory control. The company maintains a membership-based model, charging an annual fee and offering Executive memberships with rewards on qualified purchases. Ancillary services such as gasoline stations, pharmacies, food courts, and travel complement the retail business. Costco also emphasizes employee welfare as a key ethical component. The company’s fiscal year ends in late August, using a 52/53-week calendar with a notable seasonal sales peak in the winter holiday period [10-K accession 0000909832-26-000093 lines L000733-L000787].
sections.Market Positioning and Growth Outlook: Costco’s competitive positioning is based on providing members with consistently lower prices on a curated range of fast-selling items (less than 4,000 SKUs per warehouse), combining private-label and brand-name merchandise. The company controls shrinkage through limited access and membership requirements, and maintains shorter operating hours and efficient warehouse layouts to reduce labor costs. Their growth strategy includes expansion within existing markets by increasing warehouse count and entering new geographic markets, although it carries risks related to competition, regulatory hurdles, and member acquisition challenges in unfamiliar regions. Costco operates 774 gas stations as part of its ancillary business, which accounted for 11% of total net sales in 2026. The Executive membership penetration is strong, accounting for approximately 75.2% of worldwide net sales. Membership renewal rates are high (92.3% in U.S. and Canada, 89.8% worldwide), supporting a stable revenue stream from recurring fees, which totaled $5.907 billion in fiscal 2026 [10-K accession 0000909832-26-000093 lines L000733-L000784].
sections.Valuation Insights:
### Valuation Insights for Costco Wholesale Corporation (COST)

Costco's fiscal year 2026 total revenue was $303.15 billion [C:revenue] with robust year-over-year growth of 10.1% [C:revenue_growth], indicating sustained topline expansion. The company generated operating income of $11.685 billion [C:operating_income], yielding an operating margin of 3.85% [C:operating_margin], which, while positive, remains slightly below Walmart's 4.18% [C:wmt_operating_margin] and Target's 4.88% [C:tgt_operating_margin], reflecting Costco's competitive cost structure in the wholesale sector. Net income attributable to Costco was $9.226 billion [C:net_income], translating to a GAAP diluted EPS of $20.76 [C:diluted_eps].

Return on average equity stood at a high 28.4% [C:return_on_average_equity], demonstrating efficient capital utilization. The debt-to-equity ratio, including the current portion of long-term debt, was a modest 0.17 [C:debt_to_equity], underscoring a conservative leverage profile, especially when compared to peers. Free cash flow was strong at $9.382 billion [C:free_cash_flow], providing capacity for strategic investments or returns to shareholders.

From the latest quarterly earnings, net sales increased 11.2% year-over-year to $93.9 billion [C:q4_revenue], with a diluted EPS of $6.75 [C:q4_diluted_eps]. Based on a recent share price of $904.7, Costco trades at a P/E multiple of 43.58 [C:price_to_earnings], reflecting market expectations for continued growth and profitability.

Costco's focus on international expansion and digitally-enabled sales, noted in the release [L:10], may sustain topline momentum. The lower operating margin relative to peers could be a function of membership-driven pricing or cost absorption strategies, which warrants monitoring.

Insight: Costco’s reduced long-term debt level from $5.71 billion last year to $3.91 billion this year while increasing operating income suggests effective debt management paired with operational efficiency (10-K line 85) [L:10-K].
sections.Future Developments and Strategic Recomm: Costco should continue focusing on selective warehouse expansion while cautious of cannibalization effects on existing stores. Prioritizing growth in high-potential regions and further enhancing e-commerce offerings could boost market penetration. Given the significant contribution of gasoline sales and ancillary services to net sales, further investment in these areas may provide incremental revenue opportunities. Ensuring supply chain diversification and expanding private-label merchandise where quality and member value are high will help mitigate supplier risks. Monitoring membership renewal trends and Executive membership growth will remain critical. Additionally, balancing operational efficiency with employee welfare will support sustainability. Future quarterly and annual filings should be reviewed for updates on new warehouse openings, international market entries, and progress on strategic initiatives [10-K accession 0000909832-26-000093 lines L000838-L000841].
sections.Investment Recommendation: Hold provisional based on diluted EPS of $20.76 per share in fiscal 2026 [C:diluted_eps]. The company's strong profitability and growth are offset by a relatively high P/E of 43.58, and operating margin slightly below peers, indicating mixed signals regarding valuation and margin sustainability.

COSTCO WHOLESALE CORPORATION REPORTS FOURTH QUARTER AND FISCAL YEAR 2026 OPERATING RESULTS
ISSAQUAH, Wash., September 24, 2026 - Costco Wholesale Corporation (“Costco” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: COST) today announced its operating results for the 16-week fourth quarter and the 52-week fiscal year ended August 30, 2026.
Net sales for the quarter increased 11.2 percent, to $93.9 billion, from $84.4 billion last year. Net sales for the fiscal year increased 10.1 percent, to $297.2 billion, from $269.9 billion last year.
Comparable sales for the fourth quarter and fiscal year were as follows:

|  |  | Adjusted* |  |  |  | Adjusted*
U.S. | 10.7% |  | 7.2% |  | 8.2% |  | 6.6%

Other International | 7.0% |  | 6.2% |  | 9.8% |  | 6.5%
Total Company | 9.4% |  | 6.7% |  | 8.4% |  | 6.6%
Digitally-Enabled | 19.5% |  | 19.8% |  | 20.9% |  | 20.7%
*Excluding the impacts from changes in gasoline prices and foreign exchange.
Net income for the fourth quarter was $2.998 billion, $6.75 per diluted share, compared to $2.610 billion, $5.87 per diluted share, last year. This year's fourth quarter was positively impacted by a non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds received in the quarter, less partial reinvestment of those refunds in increased member values. Net income for the fiscal year was $9.226 billion, $20.76 per diluted share, compared to $8.099 billion, $18.21 per diluted share, last year.
Costco currently operates 939 warehouses, including 647 in the United States and Puerto Rico, 115 in Canada, 43 in Mexico, 37 in Japan, 29 in the United Kingdom, 20 in Korea, 15 in Australia, 14 in Taiwan, seven in China, five in Spain, three in France, two in Sweden, and one each in Iceland, and New Zealand. Costco also operates e-commerce sites in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., Mexico, Korea, Taiwan, Japan, Australia, and China.
A conference call to discuss these results is scheduled for 2:00 p.m. (PT) today, September 24, 2026, and will be available via a webcast on investor.costco.com (click “Events & Presentations”).
